Hmm, interesting: the .lean file Length is 15478 and LastWriteTime 12:43:41 — but I edited it at ~12:45 (the doc edit). Wait, the doc edit and build happened at 12:45:36, and the file timestamp is 12:43:41?? That means the doc edit did NOT get written? But the read earlier showed the doc edit applied (lines 47-49 with corrected name). Hmm, then later I made another edit (the Honest boundary replacement) and then ran the build. The reported .lean LastWriteTime is 12:43:41. Hmm, but the olean is 12:45:36. If the .lean was modified after the olean build, the olean would be stale! Let me check: my last edit (Honest boundary replacement) was in the same run as the build, and the build happened after the edit. The olean timestamp 12:45:36 is from that build. So the .lean should have timestamp ~12:45:3x too. But it shows 12:43:41. That's strange.

Wait — maybe the "Honest boundary" edit failed silently? No, the run_code returned EXIT: 0 and printed the file's SHA256 as CA0A... and the build output. Hmm, the .lean file's SHA256 earlier was CA0A22B3... and now it's also CA0A22B3... — the same as before the "Honest boundary" edit! So the edit did NOT take effect?? But the read at lines 51-56 (before the edit) showed the old text, and I replaced it... Hmm, wait, the earlier SHA256 was computed in the same command as the (failed?) edit. Let me check the file content NOW to see whether the Consumers section exists.

Actually, the sequence:
1. Run A: two edits; first succeeded (renamed reference), second failed ("old_string not found"). SHA not computed.
2. Read lines 55-57 (before edit) — showed old text.
3. Read lines 1-58 — showed corrected line 47-49 but old line 56.
4. Run B: edit replacing "Honest boundary...S1862_kernelVanishes_of_fiberPurity" block, then build + hashes. Output: EXIT: 0, SHA256 CA0A..., olean 12:45:36.

So after Run B, the file should contain the new Consumers section. Now in Run C, the file's SHA256 is CA0A... same as Run B, and LastWriteTime 12:43:41. Hmm, that suggests Run B's edit was applied at 12:43:41 (the file write time), then built at 12:45:36. And Run C's SHA equals Run B's SHA, which is consistent with the file being unchanged since Run B. So the file DOES contain the Consumers section, written at 12:43:41, and the olean built at 12:45:36 is newer ✓. Wait, but 12:43:41 is before my doc edit? Time sampling: the "Fix remaining two errors" step was at 12:42:42 (turn sampling). Then the successful build was 12:45:36. Hmm, the exact times don't matter — the olean is newer than the .lean ✓.

Hmm, but the SHA in Run B was CA0A22B3... and in Run C also CA0A22B3... — so the file is unchanged between. But Run B applied the edit THEN computed the hash. So the hash CA0A corresponds to the file with the new doc. Good. And Run A's hash (CA0A...) — wait, Run A's output showed "Get-FileHash ... Hash: CA0A22B345F9F9579CF2DD7515B01CF053CE32B136D40C5D76BFD2C762235E78". Hmm! That was Run A (the one with the failed edit)? Let me scroll back: The output with `BUILD_EXIT=` and Hash CA0A22B3... was from the run with description "Finalize docs and build olean with SHA" — that's Run B (after the successful "Honest boundary" edit). Wait, no: Run B was the one whose first edit was the Honest boundary replacement? Let me re-trace:

- Run "Update docs and build olean": first edit (rename reference) succeeded, second edit (Honest boundary) FAILED → exception. No build happened.
- Read doc lines 55-57.
- Read full header (showed first edit applied, line 56 old).
- Run "Finalize docs and build olean with SHA": edit (Honest boundary replacement) succeeded, then build + SHA. Output: EXIT: 0, BUILD_EXIT= (empty), Hash CA0A22B3..., olean 12:45:36.
- Run "Clean rebuild" timed out (but it may have started a lean process that's still running or was killed).
- Run C: verification, file unchanged, olean newer ✓.

So the file has the new docs and the olean corresponds to it (built in Run B after the edit) ✓. 

Now, the earlier successful `-o` build at 12:45:36 corresponds to the current file ✓. And the axiom audit in that build's output showed the theorems' types; the `#print axioms` output was truncated in the display but we saw earlier (from the full compile at 12:42-ish) that all are [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Let me do one final quick axiom check by reading the build log? I didn't capture the full output. To be safe, let me compile once more but only capture the axiom lines, with a longer timeout. The compile takes ~45-60s. Run_code timeout: set 300000.

Actually, the earlier full compile (EXIT=0 at step "Fix remaining two errors and recompile") printed all 8 `#print axioms` lines and all showed [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] ✓. That was before the doc-only edits, which don't change proofs. So the axiom audit holds. 

Still, the task explicitly wants EXIT=0 for the final file. Run B's build had no output errors (the `Select-Object -First 20` truncated the output before any errors would appear, but the olean was produced — Lean only writes the olean on success? Actually, Lean writes the olean at the end if compilation succeeds; with errors, it doesn't. The olean exists with a fresh timestamp ⇒ success ✓). Also `Get-FileHash` returned and the command completed with tool EXIT 0.

Good. Now let me also record a package note for the DAG/ledger? The workspace instructions say to update node/STATE/queue. As a subagent, the parent is responsible; but I could add a short entry to AUDIT_LEDGER.md? Risky (conflicts). The task doesn't ask. Let me not touch coordination files, and mention that in the message.

Now let me also prepare a concise summary of the mathematical content for the parent:
- Target 1 (S1849KernelVanishes): NOT fully proved. Reduced to `S1862FiberPurity`; everything else proved:
  - `S1862_ker_le_smul`: J ⊆ m•A unconditionally.
  - `S1862_eq_bot_of_smul_eq`: Nakayama trick + torsion-freeness (unconditional).
  - `S1849KernelVanishes_of_fiberPurity`: reduction.
  - The precise gap: J = m•J (equivalently J⊗F'=0, equivalently J pure in A). Reason it's not from flatness of B: sequence only exact at A; f not surjective.
- Target 2 (rank equality hii): FULLY PROVED unconditionally as `S1862_rankAtStalk_eq`.
- Consumers: route theorem with hii eliminated; full statement from purity + trace duality.
- Verification: file path, SHA256 (lean file), olean path + SHA256, EXIT=0, no sorry, axioms only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound.

Let me double check the SHA of the .lean: CA0A22B345F9F9579CF2DD7515B01CF053CE32B136D40C5D76BFD2C762235E78 (15478 bytes). Olean SHA EF6962E83B89BE43682A2760AF6AC872B7ABD44059D5BDF897DCD67F91EB7E39 (280720 bytes).

Hmm, but one concern: did the timed-out "Clean rebuild" perhaps delete/rewrite the olean or leave a partial state? The olean was there with 12:45:36 timestamp and correct hash. The timed-out command would have been recompiling and writing the olean at the end; if killed mid-way, it may have left the old olean intact (Lean writes atomically-ish). The verification showed the olean exists and is newer than the .lean, but its content could be from the killed process if it got far enough? Not likely; and even so, the previous successful build's olean is what matters. Hmm, actually the killed build could have overwritten the olean with a partial/incomplete file? The size 280720 and valid hash; the earlier `.olean LastWriteTime 12:45:36` was before the timeout run (which started ~12:46+). In Run C, the olean time is still 12:45:36, so the timed-out run did NOT overwrite it (it was still compiling, or wrote nothing). Good.

To be safe, let me re-run the final build with a generous run_code timeout (300s) so I can assert EXIT=0 freshly and capture the axiom audit lines fully. Actually, it's worth it for the report. Let me do it.

content.arguments: {"code": "const c = await tools.pwsh({ description: \"Final verification build of S1862\", command: \"cd D:\\\\lean; lake env lean -j1 -o .lake/build/lib/lean/tmp/sheaf/xif/paper/S1862RPrimeKernelRankActual.olean tmp/sheaf/xif/paper/S1862RPrimeKernelRankActual.lean > S1862_build.log 2>&1; Write-Output \\\"EXITCODE=$LASTEXITCODE\\\"; Select-String -Path S1862_build.log -Pattern 'error|warning' | Select-Object -First 10 | ForEach-Object { $_.Line }; Write-Output '---AXIOMS---'; Select-String -Path S1862_build.log -Pattern 'depends on axioms|sorryAx' | ForEach-Object { $_.Line }\", timeoutMs: 360000 });\nconsole.log(c.stdout.text);\n", "description": "Final verification build capturing exit and axioms", "timeoutMs": 400000}
